correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the complete census without executing the supplied scripts. The coefficient at (i,j) in the product of class sums C,D is r_C(i)c_D(j). Summing separately over D and C proves profile equality is necessary within each class, and the product formula gives sufficiency. Partition the rows by identical complete row profiles and the columns by identical complete column profiles. Every color class lies in one resulting rectangle, where it is a nonempty biregular bipartite graph. Conversely any subdivision of each such rectangle into biregular graphs with disjoint color labels gives exactly the chosen row and column profile partitions: rows in different row blocks have disjoint nonempty supports, and likewise for columns. In an m-by-n profile rectangle a nonzero class size is divisible by both m and n, so coprime rectangles cannot split. The only potentially splittable sizes here are 2-by-2 (two complementary matchings, one possible partition) and 3-by-3. The latter can split as a matching and its complement (six choices) or as three matchings (two choices: the complement of any matching is a six-cycle with unique unordered alternating matching split). There are 25 unsplit labeled partitions, nine diagonal splits from the 2+1 by 2+1 profile choices and eight splits of the whole square. Under independent row and column permutations the 25 products give nine types and the three split forms give one further type each. For the three-matching partition, normalize one matching to the diagonal; the other two are the two 3-cycles. The class counts and labeled orbit sizes from these forms give the exact displayed table, with rank counts 1,12,4,9,9,6,1 for ranks 1,2,3,4,5,6,9. The automorphism group is exactly the independent row and column permutations, since left and right translations distinguish row and column coordinates. Automorphic realization holds by the product of the full symmetric groups inside each profile block for unsplit products, the simultaneous flip of the paired rows and columns for the 2-by-2 split, simultaneous S3 after normalizing a 3-by-3 matching with its complement, and simultaneous cyclic shifts for three matchings. Each named group has the required class orbits. These cover all cases and confirm the 42/12/25/17 census independently of the frozen outputs.
residual_risks: Conclusion is over Q with multiplication closure alone and natural semigroup automorphisms; transposition is excluded and no general larger-band claim is tested.

value.rationale: The motivating semigroup results establish products yet explicitly leave additional Schur rings on rectangular bands. The first square outside the two-row family and the order-seven semigroup census is a meaningful cutoff, not a random nine-element example. The finding resolves the exact gap beyond products, shows that it is nonetheless exhausted by automorphism orbits, and supplies rank and orbit data a larger band classification can test against. The small size makes a transparent structural certificate possible, not the result a known table recomputation.
residual_risks: No implication that larger rectangular bands are automorphic or governed by these three split types.
